record.prompt: If we switch the log shippers to encrypted connections, do we have any published numbers showing they'll cope with 50k lines a second?

input.query: log shipper throughput encrypted TLS lines per second benchmark
логшиппер пропускная способность шифрование TLS нагрузка

record.final_answer:
No — we don't have any numbers, published or measured.

What's actually in hand:

- /stand/ws has only README.md and config/agent.yaml, one commit ("initial"). No benchmark notes, no load-test output, no vendor doc excerpts. Grep for benchmark/throughput/TLS finds only the README's "Peak volume: 50,000 lines per second" and the `tls: false` line in the config.
- Nothing in memory about Marrowlog throughput.
- I can't check the vendor's published figures from here either — no DNS/network in this environment (`marrowlog.com` and `collector.int.example` both fail to resolve). So even if the vendor publishes a number, I can't confirm it exists or what it says.

And a vendor number wouldn't settle it anyway, because of the size of what we're asking for. At 50k lines/s × ~900 B, each agent pushes:

    45.0 MB/s  ≈ 360 Mbit/s sustained  (~3.9 TB/day if it ran at peak all day)
    500-line batches arrive at ~100 batches/s

That's a continuously saturated ~360 Mbps stream from a sidecar with 1 vCPU reserved. TLS itself isn't the scary part — handshakes are per-connection, not per-line, and AES-NI bulk encryption runs in the hundreds of MB/s per core — but you're adding per-byte CPU work onto a core that is already likely the binding constraint, plus record framing and larger write/syscall pressure. Whether it holds at 50k depends on that specific agent build, so it needs a measurement, not a citation.

To get a real answer, one load test on a representative VM profile (1 vCPU, 900 B lines, peak rate) comparing plain TCP vs TLS: watch achieved lines/s, agent CPU, p99 send latency, and whether the disk buffer spills (`buffer.disk: false` today, so backpressure goes straight to the app). If you want, I can write the test harness and the exact pass/fail thresholds — but I'd need a reachable collector endpoint or a local TLS listener to test against.
